extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in number theory / arithmetic geometry; readers following the Mochizuki–Scholze–Stix IUTT controversy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and substantive mathematical standards for assessing Inter‑Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUTT) claims and critiques (especially the Scholze–Stix report) — what hypotheses/data a valid analysis must include and how to judge objections. Geared toward researchers checking correctness of mathematical arguments and assumptions in this controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting a proof requires complete understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: If Mochizuki’s proof has to be rejected, then it must be based on a complete understanding of its ideas and present correct mathematical arguments, precisely identifying the issue(s) with its claimed strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques should not rest on partial readings, heuristic objections, or authority; they must (a) fully understand the ideas involved, and (b) give precise mathematical arguments pinpointing the defect(s). See § 1.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remember geometric base-points for tempered fundamental groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s Key Principle of Inter‑Universality requires remembering the geometric base‑points for tempered fundamental groups — i.e., one must work with Πtemp_{X/E;K} (with a K‑geometric base point) and not with Πtemp_{X/E} alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses that ignore the geometric base‑point datum (the algebraically closed complete valued field K and its untilt/tilting data) fail to capture the input data Mochizuki uses; see § 1.2.1 and the comparison table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include perfectoid and tilting/untilt data (not just cardinality)
rubrics_metrics.description: When working with perfectoid/algebraically closed fields K as geometric base‑points one must include tilting/untilt data (untilts) rather than thinking the isomorphism class is determined by cardinality alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caution: the isomorphism class of algebraically closed perfectoid fields K ⊃ Q_p is not determined by cardinality; adequate input data must record untilt/tilting information. See the Caution following § 1.2.1 and reference to Joshi, 2022 Definition 5.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anabelian reconstruction does not determine the perfectoid base field
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s reconstruction theorem (Mochizuki 2015, Theorem 1.9) using Πtemp_{X/E;K} determines the isomorphism class of X/E but does not determine K (the algebraically closed perfectoid field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore one cannot use that theorem alone to conclude the absence of 'arithmetic holomorphic structures' or to dismiss data required by IUTT; see § 1.2.3 and § 1.2.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of the Absolute Grothendieck Conjecture does not imply impossibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity (or invalidity) of the Absolute Grothendieck Conjecture for hyperbolic curves does not imply Mochizuki’s proof is impossible; existence of the Teichmüller‑type structures Mochizuki claims is independent of that conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques that conflate anabelian/reconstruction results with impossibility of IUTT are misunderstanding the independence of Teichmüller‑type geometric constructions; see § 1.2.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct Hodge‑Theaters arise from distinct geometric/arithmetic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Hodge‑Theaters (with fixed decoration) can be isomorphic as abstract objects, distinct Hodge‑Theaters legitimately arise from distinct geometric and arithmetic data and one must not ignore that arithmetic/geometric origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label‑forgetful identifications that ignore underlying arithmetic/geometric decorations erase the very variation needed in Mochizuki’s arguments; see § 1.2.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mochizuki’s formalism should be read as a proxy for p‑adic Hodge theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s definitions and formalism (including perfect Frobenioids and their realifications) function as an approximate proxy for modern p‑adic Hodge Theory across primes; critiques should recognise and compare to standard p‑adic Hodge machinery (e.g., tilting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissals claiming the definitions are purposeless are incorrect if they ignore this proxy relationship; see § 1.2.6 and the remarks on perfect Frobenioids vs perfectoids (Joshi, 2024b appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: A valid critique must include all required input hypotheses (valuation/log/theta data)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Scholze‑Stix critique omitted key mathematical assumptions and aspects of Mochizuki’s Theory (e.g., geometric base‑points, valuation data, log‑Links, Theta‑Links, distinct arithmetic holomorphic structures); a correct analysis must explicitly include these hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comparison table (§ 1.3) lists these objects and shows where Scholze‑Stix ignored or misidentified domains/codomains; any rebuttal must account for the full hypothesis set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot build theory using arbitrary geometric base‑points but working only over Q̄_p
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot validly require arbitrary geometric base‑points for tempered fundamental groups yet perform the theory solely over Q̄_p; the theory must allow arbitrary algebraically closed perfectoid base fields (or equivalent data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi asserts his work fixes this central issue by including arbitrary alg. closed perfectoid fields in the data of an arithmeticoid; see NOTE (2) in § 1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate existence and deformation properties for objects you assert cannot exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If claiming objects (e.g., distinct Hodge‑Theaters, arithmetic holomorphic structures) cannot exist, one must supply a proof; conversely, assertions of existence should be demonstrated (locally and globally) and show deformation properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi claims to demonstrate existence and deformation (e.g., via arbitrary alg. closed perfectoid fields or valuation data and via Frobenius rather than proxies); critiques that merely assert impossibility without constructing counterexamples are inadequate. See § 1.2.5 and § 1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group‑theoretic (anabelian) methods have reconstruction limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods relying purely on group‑theoretic anabelian reconstruction cannot reconstruct the algebraically closed perfectoid field (e.g., C_p) from the topological absolute Galois group G_{Q_p}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore conclusions that ignore the geometric base‑point datum or assume reconstruction of K from group data are flawed; see § 1.2.1 and references to Mochizuki 1997.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain fairness and mathematical professionalism in critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Critiques and public commentary on complex mathematical claims should be fair, precise, and professional; avoid unprofessional behavior (name‑calling, personal insults) and ensure mathematical objections are presented clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joshi emphasizes fairness in his own critiques (§ 1.1) and condemns unprofessional reactions by others; scholarly discourse should focus on clear mathematical argumentation (Conclusion, point (4)).
